newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower, flatten in early trade.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower, flatten in early trade.

text.p: French stocks opened lower on Friday, then turned flat in thin trading with many investors clinging to the sidelines amid election uncertainty.

"Investors will steer clear until the election. The risk, in terms of market valuation, is too great. Better wait a month and find out what France's direction will be," said one trader. "Until then, we'll be driven by the polls."
An IPSOS poll showing the ruling conservative coalition would get a wafer-thin majority weighed on French financial markets on Thursday afternoon. The two-round election is on May 25 and June 1.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 1.70 points, or 0.07 perent, at 2,541.53 at 0840 GMT. It had opened at 2,527.35, weighed by lower bond prices, Wall Street's fall and weakness in the dollar and the franc.
The CAC-40 April futures contract was up five at 2,543.
Volume was a thin 300 million francs.
Pharmaceutical shares firmed on speculation that Roche may be building a war chest with a view to an acquisition.

Synthelabo shares rose 3.5 percent to 680 francs, as it is viewed as a possible target. Synthelabo declined comment but L'Oreal said this week it considered its controlling stake in Synthelabo a handsome investment and was under no pressure to decide whether to stay in the pharmaceuticals business or quit.
Shares in Elf Aquitaine's Sanofi drugs unit rose 2.51 percent at 530 francs. Elf has said it would entertain a sale.

Eurotunnel shares rose 2.31 percent to 6.65 francs. The Channel Tunnel operator said on Thursday it had clinched an agreement with lead banks to restructure its debt, a deal which it said would make it financially secure for the next six years.
